hook.text: You use your warehouse for storage. You could rent it out for $5,000 a month. That's your opportunity cost.

buildup.text: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative you give up when making a choice.

discovery.text: It doesn't appear in accounting records, but it's real—and ignoring it leads to bad decisions.

twist.text: A college degree has an opportunity cost: the four years of salary you gave up while studying.

climax.text: Every resource has an alternative use. Effective managers factor in what they're sacrificing.

punchline.text: What you chose to skip is part of what your choice cost.

quiz.question: What is opportunity cost?
options: The value of the next best alternative given up
The price of the cheapest option
A cost that occurs in the future

details.summary: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone when a decision is made. This topic explains why opportunity costs don't appear in accounting records but are essential for sound managerial decision-making.
details.whyItMatters: Every choice has an opportunity cost. Ignoring it means you might choose options that look profitable on paper but actually destroy value compared to what you could have done instead.
takeaways: Opportunity cost is the benefit lost by not choosing the next best alternative
It never appears in financial statements but is critical for internal decision-making
Using capacity to produce Product A has an opportunity cost equal to the profit lost from not producing Product B

faq.question: What is opportunity cost in management accounting?
faq.answer: Opportunity cost is the potential benefit you give up when you choose one alternative over another. If a factory uses its capacity to produce widgets instead of gadgets, the profit from the forgone gadgets is the opportunity cost of producing widgets.

faq.question: Why isn't opportunity cost recorded in the accounting books?
faq.answer: Accounting records document actual transactions that occurred, not hypothetical alternatives. Opportunity cost represents the value of a path not taken, so there's no transaction to record. It exists only in analysis, not in the general ledger.
